summary:
Turn 8 opened a new Candidate on the recovery value selection, found while working the accept-status premise, and kept that premise open as its own question.

The lead. startRecoveryForInstance seeds the leader bookkeeping with lb.ballot = the record's old vbal, then makes a new ballot and assigns inst.bal and inst.vbal to that new ballot before building its own PrepareReply, so the self entry reports the newly made ballot as its VBallot. handlePrepareReply adopts a reply's attributes while element.VBallot >= lb.ballot and raises lb.ballot as it iterates, so the self entry can raise the running maximum above every remote reply that holds the committed or accepted value at an older vbal. The question is whether that makes the recovering replica ignore a remote COMMITTED reply and proceed from its local record (sub-case 6 restart, NOOP when no local command is known) instead of re-proposing the committed vector — which would be agreement-relevant, because a replica that already installed the commit returns early on a later Commit while the recoverer and its accept peers commit a different vector.

Framing and evidence discipline. The question is filed as an A2 relationship question (the ballot context each reply carries decides which value a leadership transfer may adopt), with F6-ballot-priority as the principal fact, B9-recovery-trigger as the selected behavior, and B11/B10/B6/B5 as named support so the selection loop, the remote acceptor's reported vbal, the installed commit's vbal and the accept-phase vbal all stay visible. Counterevidence records that the seed ordering is what lets the self entry raise the maximum, that a remote replica only raises its bal and reports its stored vbal, that makeBallot can also return a ballot below the local vbal (owner case, IsLeader false under the launched configuration) which would invert the skipping, and that the committed command is adopted only when that element passes the vbal test. Unknowns fix the discriminators: whether the self entry is always the first passing element, whether makeBallot can regress, whether any sub-case other than the phase-1 restart is selectable for a local NONE record, and whether the intended semantics is that the recovering replica reports its old vbal.

Frontier. The accept-status Candidate remains open as a separate responsibility, with its counterevidence sharpened (the leader-side accept branch is the only place ACCEPTED is produced, so sub-case 2 is reachable through a recovering replica's own record, while an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command). No map object was changed, so the map basis stays at v4 and the existing B9/B11 unknowns continue to describe the same recovery responsibilities.
